structural_evidence.interpretation: Glycine backbone exposure (19.9%) reflects solvent-accessible declivity, not buried void. Total SASA increase (+76) is 3x SMALLER than L99A (+242). No persistent structural debt.

sasa_threshold_framework_v2.note: For non-glycine mutations. Glycine backbone REL requires separate interpretation.
sasa_threshold_framework_v2.REL_3_to_8: Partial void, local accommodation → weak/no exchange (F153A = 4.5%)
sasa_threshold_framework_v2.REL_10_to_20_non_glycine: Persistent buried void → DYNAMIC if CAN > threshold (L99A = 15.2%)
sasa_threshold_framework_v2.glycine_special_case: Glycine REL reflects backbone exposure. Must combine with total SASA change and literature. L99G: +76 Å² total SASA (small) + solvent-accessible declivity = ENERGETIC despite 19.9% REL.

triad_falsification.falsification_from_F153A: F153A removes MORE volume than L99A (-68 to -74 vs -57 Å³) but shows 3.4x LOWER mutation-site REL and MORE compact global SASA → volume loss alone is insufficient
triad_falsification.falsification_from_L99G: L99G removes EVEN MORE volume than L99A (-76 vs -57 Å³) but creates solvent-accessible declivity, not buried void → burial and scaffold rigidity are the key variables
triad_falsification.conclusion: The naive hypothesis is falsified from TWO INDEPENDENT DIRECTIONS. PERA's refined hypothesis (structural debt exceeding local accommodation capacity) survives.
